articles.title: Astronaut Photographs a Patch of 'Moon Rock' on Earth
articles.summary: From the space station, an astronaut snapped a bright formation in Madagascar made of anorthosite, the same kind of rock that forms the Moon's bright highlands.

articles.title: Neanderthal Glue May Have Doubled as Germ-Fighting Medicine
articles.summary: Scientists recreated birch tar, a sticky glue Neanderthals used for tools, and found that every sample slowed the growth of bacteria that infect wounds.

articles.title: Colors and Gases Could Help Scientists Find Tiny Alien Life
articles.summary: Scientists studying tough microbes high above Earth think pigments, gases and hardy cells could guide the search for single-celled life on Venus, Mars and faraway planets.
